articles.title: Gargoyle
articles.summary: Dark olive-charcoal diagonal weave, matte and mottled, like weathered stone or old canvas. Reads as a muted charcoal-olive military grey with a faint diagonal weave; the green line is barely visible and the car looks like old canvas or stone.
articles.what: Up close: Dull olive-grey cloth-like diamond lattice, soft diagonals about 12-16 px per diamond, with a fine grain. One faint green glowing swoosh crosses the tile like a wing outline, peaking near the middle. From a distance: Reads as a muted charcoal-olive military grey with a faint diagonal weave; the green line is barely visible and the car looks like old canvas or stone. Measured spec (average): metal 20, roughness 93, coat 51. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, dirt late model, stock car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Gargoyle on the hood".
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body panels and bumpers: even weave works as a base
The faint green arc is one placed motif in the tile and may show as a wing-like line on a big panel
White, orange or sand numbers read; grey and olive ones vanish.
Fine light linework or thin stripes: stay readable on the dull ground
Pairs well with: black, gunmetal, orange, sand.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not weathered stone or rock: the render is a woven diamond lattice
Not metallic: metal none
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, delicate thin pinstripes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 20 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 93 (satin gloss), clearcoat 51 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, delicate thin pinstripes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine light linework or thin stripes: stay readable on the dull ground; orange or sand accents and graphics: pair well per palette
Patterns to avoid: weave, carbon, grids: moire with the diamonds; camo: muddy
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat strip: contrast against the satin cloth; fine metal flake: adds a hint of glint
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
